Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem. Think of it like looking up a word in a dictionary that uses the word itself in its definition, but you keep looking up the definition until you find a base case. Every recursive function needs a base case—a condition that stops the recursion—otherwise it will loop forever. By breaking a big problem into smaller, identical pieces, recursion can make complex tasks like traversing trees or calculating factorials elegantly simple.
